title: Ethiopian Beef and Lentil Stew
localName: ሥጋ ምስር ወጥ — Siga Misir Wat
community: All of Ethiopia — the combined protein wat
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Beef and Lentil Stew — a combination of cubed beef and red lentils cooked together in a berbere sauce. The lentils extend the beef, thicken the sauce naturally, and add plant protein to produce a complete, economical, deeply nourishing stew.
longDesc: Siga Misir Wat is the practical family wat — combining the flavour and prestige of beef with the economy and nutrition of red lentils. The lentils dissolve partially into the sauce, thickening it naturally and adding their protein to the beef.
steps: Add kibbeh and berbere. Toast 3 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger. Add beef. Coat.
Lentils should dissolve and thicken the sauce.
chefTips: Add lentils after the beef is half-cooked — they need only 25—30 minutes.
Red lentils dissolve — creating a naturally thick sauce.
commonMistakes: Adding lentils too early — they disintegrate before the beef is tender.
cookingScience: Red lentils have had their seed coat removed — this allows them to absorb water and dissolve much faster than whole lentils. The dissolved lentil starch and protein thickens the sauce naturally.
sustainabilityTips: Lentils extend beef — more sustainable use of animal protein.
healthBenefits: Complete protein from beef and lentils together.
culturalNote: Beef and lentil stew is the Ethiopian cook's practical wisdom — stretching the prestige of beef with the economy of lentils, producing a dish more nutritious and more satisfying than either alone.
